rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely unknown, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. This experiment tests a simple RNA-only model with singleprofile and PCA encoding, isolating the effect of RNA modality and basic representation. It clarifies whether RNA data alone can achieve reasonable performance, providing a reference point for comparing more complex multimodal configurations later.

The existing evidence shows that using singleprofile with no aggregation achieves 0.48 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether using multiprofile with avgpool aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It is the best next step as it builds on the baseline while exploring key design choices with minimal parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile (config_001). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (config_002) with transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It builds on the promising multiprofile direction while exploring a key design choice with minimal changes.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.590664 accuracy) outperform singleprofile and transformer aggregation variants. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from PCA_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) while keeping multiprofile and avgpool settings would improve accuracy. This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, and builds on the promising multiprofile direction.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6501). This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It is the best use of the next experiment as it exploits the promising scvi_n200 + multiprofile direction while exploring a key design choice with minimal changes.

The existing evidence shows that rna_only models with scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting achieve the highest accuracy (0.652970). This experiment tests adding image data (multimodal) with the same RNA encoder and aggregation method (avgpool) to isolate the effect of multimodal fusion. It balances exploration of multimodal potential with exploitation of the proven scvi_n200 RNA encoder.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006, 0.653 accuracy) are the best so far. This experiment tests a multimodal extension using the same RNA encoder (scvi_n200) with resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion. It isolates the effect of adding image data to the best RNA-only configuration, balancing exploitation of current strengths with exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models with transformer aggregation and concat fusion (config_032, 0.6878 accuracy) are strong. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_033) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion method. It's a logical extension of the current top-performing configuration, balancing exploitation of promising directions with refinement of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_033) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests whether combining scgpt (RNA encoder) and imagenet_vit_l (image encoder) with the same transformer aggregation and weighted fusion could further improve performance. It isolates the impact of advanced encoders while leveraging proven aggregation/fusion strategies, maximizing the chance to surpass the current best with the final budget.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_033) achieve high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping other components the same, isolating the impact of the image encoder. It is the best use of the final experiment to validate if the stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) could further improve performance, directly building on the most promising configuration.
